To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression ratio for an ORF is equal (within the experimental error) to the ratio of its protein copy numbers, and that the expression ratio profile for a particular ORFs versus time of culture can be related to changes in its copy number per cell.

the ratio of expression levels for an ORF in two strains of bacteria, measured by microarray analysis, is equal to the corresponding ratio of the copy number of the encoded protein and that the expression ratio of an ORF in a batch culture of bacteria is equal to the relative number of copies of the protein per cell at any time during the culture.

the expression ratio of a gene obtained by microarray is equal to the protein ratio for the encoded protein and that the expression ratio versus culture time for a particular OR F can be related to changes in relative numbers of copies per cell of the encoded protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a mathematical framework that links the molecular processes involved with transcription, translation, cell division and growth with the properties of bacterial cells and the measurements obtained by microarray technology.
the development of a quantitative theoretical framework that links the molecular processes of transcription and translation of a particular ORF with the properties of the cells in a population.
the development of a quantitative framework for the interpretation of gene expression data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microarray analysis is an excellent tool for the identification of genes that are expressed at a particular stage in the growth cycle of a bacterial cell.
the microarray measurements were in agreement with the theoretical framework and the conclusions drawn were in agreement with previous experimental studies.
the expression ratio for a particular ORFs obtained by microarray measurements is equal to the copy number ratio of that protein in the cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theoretical framework presented here provides a quantitative basis for the interpretation of the data obtained from microarray experiments.
the analysis of microarrays based on our theoretical framework provides information that is complementary to that obtained by other approaches.

the theory provides a quantitative framework for the interpretation of the results of microarray experiments, and that this framework can be used to obtain information about the growth of a population of bacterial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theory can be used to analyse microarray data to gain a deeper understanding of how bacteria adapt to different growth environments.
a theoretical framework for the analysis of gene expression data has been developed and applied to microarray data for the study of the growth of M.  tuberculosis.
the microarray expression ratio for an ORF can be interpreted in a quantitative way in terms of the relative copy numbers of the protein encoded by the ORF.
